context_requirements: Thrombin (F2) signalling is a coagulation cascade function; the assayed lines are immortalised adherent tumour lines that do not express the full coagulation cascade or PAR-activating thrombin
Response would require functional thrombin generation or exogenous thrombin signalling, neither of which is supplied by a thrombin inhibitor alone
Direct thrombin inhibitors such as dabigatran show anti-inflammatory/anti-glial effects only in intact CNS tissue, not in cultured tumour lines
falsifiers: Reproducible concentration-dependent changes in landmark gene expression at 6 h or 24 h in any of the nine lines
Induction of a coherent coagulation- or PAR-signalling transcriptional signature
Consistent F2-dependent gene expression changes across multiple lines

evidence.supports: Direct thrombin inhibitor dabigatran reduced glial activation markers in vivo, but effects were tissue-context dependent and not observed as a general transcriptional response in cultured cells

Thrombin inhibitor PN-1 expression in fibroblasts is regulated by IL-1 and dexamethasone, indicating thrombin-inhibitor transcriptional effects require inflammatory cytokine context absent in this assay
